propositions: A stalled git fetch connection that sends zero bytes hangs until the 300s wall-clock timeout instead of aborting on throughput starvation within seconds.
The git argv in _fetch_origin lacks http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime config, leaving the curl handle unbounded by throughput and bounded only by wall time.
A transient low-speed abort should be retried in-process a bounded number of times to self-heal within the review cycle, rather than deferring to backfill.
A legitimately slow but progressing fetch below the throughput floor should not be aborted, discriminating throughput-keyed abort from wall-clock timeout.
repo_snapshot.py at 788/800 LOC has no room for the fix and must be split along the git-subprocess cluster boundary into a new git_fetch.py module.
